page: The OVHcloud r2-240 is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel x86_64 processor based on the Haswell architecture, running at 2.2 GHz. The configuration includes 16 dedicated physical cores with no hyperthreading, supported by 16 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 240 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 15 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 400 GB SSD, and network connectivity is rated at a 10 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance tradeoff. Single-core CPU performance is weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively, reflecting the older Haswell architecture. However, multi-core performance is average, as shown by stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core benchmarks. Memory read bandwidth is average at 909.75 GB/sec cached and 40.15 GB/sec uncached, though uncached write bandwidth is weak at 21.66 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance remain in the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r2-240 offers high memory density without the premium associated with newer CPU architectures. This makes it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded compute power. It is well-suited for in-memory caching, database hosting, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks, whereas it is poorly suited for single-threaded applications or LLM inference.
